name: Afghanistan (Kingdom, 1928)
description: Three horizontal stripes of black, red and green with a white emblem in the centre: a mosque within a rayed star surrounded by wheat sheaves.
history: Short-lived horizontal version of the black, red and green tricolour introduced by King Amanullah Khan in 1928, reportedly inspired by the flags he had seen on his tour of Europe that year; the mosque emblem is surrounded by wheat, appearing on an Afghan flag for the first time. Within weeks it was rearranged as vertical stripes, the pattern kept by most Afghan flags since.
